Subject: Non-prod region split — quick clarifications

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a couple of follow-ups from our security & compliance team before we sign off on the pilot: a short list focused on non-production (staging/sandbox) tenants and private connectivity. Can you confirm the following?

1) For EU customers, does non-prod (staging, test) data remain hosted entirely within EU-bound infrastructure by default, or is it colocated with US non-prod?
2) Do you offer a private deployment option (VPC peering or PrivateLink) for non-prod? If so, please describe the connectivity model and whether any control plane traffic crosses regions.
3) KMS: are customer keys region-scoped and partitioned by account/region? Any cross-region key escrow or replication?
4) Under what circumstances would non-prod data egress to a different region (e.g., failover, snapshot restore)? Please call out logging/retention for such events.

We also need a simple network diagram and a one-page SOC 2 summary that references where non-prod is in/out of scope. Quick turnaround appreciated — can you get something over by EOD PT tomorrow?

Best,

Hi Anika —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short SOC2 summary, a VPC segmentation diagram, and KMS partition notes (see attachments). If you need any of these as signed statements for CAIQ rows we can produce a one-paragraph attestation within 48 hours.

1) Region placement: For EU customers using our hosted offering, non-prod workloads for EU tenants are deployed into EU regions (primarily eu-central-1) by default. We do not colocate EU non-prod with US non-prod unless the customer explicitly selects a cross-region option during onboarding.

2) Private connectivity: We support both VPC peering (customer-managed peering into a Redwood-managed VPC in the requested region) and PrivateLink-style private endpoints. Control plane traffic for hosted customers uses our control plane in the region with TLS and mTLS to the data plane; control plane metadata routing does not traverse outside the selected region for EU-hosted tenants. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package) the control plane can be customer-hosted in-region to avoid cross-region control plane hops.

3) KMS: Keys are region-scoped and we offer per-tenant key partitioning. For hosted customers we store keys in the cloud provider KMS in the same region as the data plane. Cross-region key replication is not enabled by default; it is only available as an opt-in DR configuration and, if enabled, keys are replicated with customer consent and logged. We also support HSM-backed keys for enterprise plans.

4) Cross-region egress: The only automatic cross-region traffic for non-prod is during a customer-requested DR test or failover; snapshot exports to external tooling (S3) are region-local by default. Any cross-region transfer is logged, labeled in our audit trail, and included in the SOC 2 logs retention policy.

Attachments in this message: caldera_soc2_summary.pdf (summary), vpc-nonprod-segmentation.png (diagram), kms-partitioning-notes.txt (technical notes).

If useful, Rishi can add the short runbook steps and the exact logging retention durations. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow to walk the team through the runbook.

Thanks,

Hi Anika — adding the technical specifics Marissa promised, pasted below for visibility.

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 1) Region placement: For EU customers using our hosted offering, non-prod workloads for EU tenants are deployed into EU regions (primarily eu-central-1) by default.

Technical details:
- Non-prod runs in dedicated regional subnets. There is no default cross-region snapshot replication for non-prod images.
- Backups: automated backups are region-local; cross-region backups are only created when a customer enables cross-region DR; those exports are encrypted in transit and at rest.
- Key rotation & HSM: We rotate KMS keys on a default 90-day policy for managed keys; enterprise HSM customer keys can be rotated on customer schedule.
- Audit logs: All cross-region transfer events are tagged with an event ID and persisted to our audit lake for 2 years by default (configurable on enterprise plans).

If you want the exact log column names and sample API calls we can paste those into the runbook link I uploaded: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-caldera-nonprod-runbook

Anika — attaching a hand-drawn network diagram and a short note that callers out the path names. Quick points:
- VPC peering option: customer peer -> customer-managed AZ -> Redwood-managed data plane in eu-central-1. No transit through US.
- PrivateLink option: consumes ENIs in-region; traffic terminates within the EU region and never traverses our US backbone for EU-hosted customers.
- Failover flow: if a customer triggers cross-region failover we create a temporary, audited egress path; automation flags the event and tags it as DR:cross-region in the audit trail.
